message.content:
In Texas, tenants have several statutory protections and responsibilities under the Texas Property Code (Title 8, Chapter 92). Below is an overview of key rights you typically enjoy as a renter: | Category | Typical Tenant Rights | Notes | |----------|-----------------------|-------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may collect a security deposit up to one month’s rent for residential units; two months for furnished units.
• Must be returned within 30 days after lease ends, minus deductions for damages beyond normal wear & tear. | Landlords must itemize deductions and provide receipts if requested. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must maintain premises in a safe, sanitary condition.
• Must repair major structural issues, plumbing, heating, electrical, etc., within a reasonable time. | “Reasonable” is often interpreted as within 30 days for major repairs. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • You’re entitled to peaceful use of the property without unreasonable interference from landlord or other tenants. | Landlord cannot enter without notice unless emergency. | | **Notice Requirements** | • For non‑renewal or termination of month‑to‑month tenancy: 30 days’ written notice.
• For eviction due to nonpayment: 3 days’ notice to pay or vacate.
• For entry: 24‑hour written notice for non‑emergency visits. | Notice must be in writing and delivered personally or via certified mail. | | **Rent Increases** | • No limit on how much rent can increase, but must give proper notice (usually 30 days for month‑to‑month). | Some cities have local ordinances limiting increases during COVID‑19 or for certain properties. | | **Discrimination Protections** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income (e.g., public assistance). | This is enforced by the Fair Housing Act and Texas Civil Rights Act. | | **Repair and Deduct / Rent Withhold** | • If landlord fails to make necessary repairs, you may (1) repair and deduct cost from rent, (2) withhold rent until repaired, or (3) terminate lease. | Must follow strict procedures: notify landlord in writing, allow reasonable time to fix, keep receipts. | | **Lease Terms** | • Lease agreements must be in writing for leases longer than one year.
• Certain clauses (e.g., “no pets”) can be challenged if they violate fair housing laws. | Oral agreements can still be enforceable but harder to prove. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must file a complaint in district court and serve a summons.
• Court will issue a judgment and order for possession if you fail to comply. | Evictions can be delayed by COVID‑19 moratoriums or local ordinances. | | **Utilities** | • Landlord must provide hot water, electricity, gas, and sewage services.
• Tenants may be responsible for utilities depending on lease terms. | Check lease for utility responsibilities. | ### How to Protect Your Rights 1. **Read Your Lease Carefully** – Understand all obligations, including pet policies, maintenance responsibilities, and notice periods. 2. **Document Everything** – Keep copies of notices, emails, text messages, and photos of any damage or maintenance issues. 3. **Use Written Notices** – Send all communications in writing (email or certified mail) to create a paper trail. 4. **Know Local Ordinances** – Some Texas cities (e.g., Austin, Dallas, Houston) have additional tenant protections such as rent control or eviction moratoria. 5. **Seek Legal Assistance** – If you face eviction or disputes, consider contacting a local tenant advocacy group or attorney. --- #### Want a Sample Lease? If you’d like a sample residential lease tailored to Texas law, let me know the parties involved and any special provisions you need (e.g., pet policy, parking, subletting). I can generate a draft using the `generate_contract` function.
